nodes.label: Shared Frame-Based Timeline
nodes.rationale: Visual code and soundtrack generation import the same frame constants so duplicate timestamps cannot drift apart; timeline.ts is the timing source of truth.

nodes.label: Visible Event Sound Mapping
nodes.rationale: Every sound cue must explain a visible event, and the quietest sound design that still communicates the story is preferred.

nodes.label: Continuous Transforming Score
nodes.rationale: Music stays continuous across scene changes and changes harmony, rhythm, texture, and energy so narrative progress feels connected rather than like a restarted track.

nodes.label: Persistent UI Spatial Continuity
nodes.rationale: Global animation phase, scale, position, clocks, counters, state, and drift persist across scene boundaries to prevent visible jumps.

nodes.label: Composition-Level Reaction Overlays
nodes.rationale: Persistent reactions live above scene-local UI so edits do not truncate their independent hold-and-fade lifecycles.

nodes.label: Deterministic Animation
nodes.rationale: A render must not change because of unseeded randomness, including reaction spacing and procedural motion.

nodes.label: Multi-Aspect Campaign Reuse
nodes.rationale: Aspect-ratio variants share timeline, audio, copy, and scene components while format-specific geometry is isolated so social tuning cannot silently alter the landscape master.

nodes.label: Archival Master Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Archival masters use PNG intermediates, high-bit-depth 4:4:4 mezzanine video, explicit BT.709 metadata, and uncompressed audio; compressed deliverables are made from the composition or master rather than another compressed derivative.

nodes.label: Remotion Video Package
nodes.rationale: The local product-video package is intentionally separate from the production Next.js application.

nodes.label: H.264 Upload Export
nodes.rationale: The upload export is a smaller high-quality derivative for services with upload limits and is recreated from the composition or master.

nodes.label: Preview Export
nodes.rationale: Preview exports optimize review speed and are not delivery masters.

nodes.label: Original Procedural Soundtrack
nodes.rationale: The build-generated WAV uses mathematical oscillators and deterministic noise only, avoiding stock music, loops, recordings, samples, and third-party audio assets.

nodes.label: Thumbnail Frame 1230
nodes.rationale: Exporting the settled celebration state from a real composition frame keeps still-image typography and visual language aligned with the trailer.

nodes.label: Viewer Loss Sequence
nodes.rationale: The six losses use a deliberate three-loss, pause, three-loss rhythm to communicate setback without lengthening the scene.

nodes.label: Bomb Reveal Recovery
nodes.rationale: The rapid 4-to-10 recovery belongs to the Clipify bomb reveal and uses lighter notes than later viewer-gain chimes.

nodes.label: Illustrative Stream Activity
nodes.rationale: Negative and positive reaction bubbles are illustrative stream activity rather than measured product data.

nodes.label: Cross-Scene Reaction Lifecycles
nodes.rationale: Recovery, negative, and positive reactions are composition-level overlays whose independent fades survive scene boundaries instead of snapping away.

nodes.label: Final Emoji Celebration
nodes.rationale: The final emoji field is one grouped celebration covered by one achievement chord; subtle breathing, floating, and wiggling keep the long hold alive without fourteen separate sound cues.

nodes.label: Global OBS Mock Drift
nodes.rationale: The OBS mock drift uses the global visual frame so its phase remains continuous across scene boundaries.
